title: kv-cache: improve memory defragmentation and spillover eviction heuristics (v6)
author: Ethan Brooks
description:
Motivation: cache fragmentation and aggressive spillover have been a recurring source of tail-latency and memory pressure in high-concurrency workloads. This PR iterates on the eviction/defragmentation heuristics to reduce excessive paging and prioritize in-place defragmentation when it provides clear cost/latency benefits. The changes are targeted at the serving runtime's KV cache and scheduler so they apply across hosted and dedicated deployments.

Summary of changes: - Introduce a fragmentation score per slab that combines free-run ratio, fragmentation age, and recent allocation churn. - Revise the spillover threshold: prefer async spill-to-disk for cold, low-churn slabs; prefer in-memory defrag for hot slabs with moderate fragmentation. - Add a throttled defrag scheduler that respects request-critical priority lanes and can opportunistically defrag during idle GPU cycles. - Make spillover I/O asynchronous with backpressure-aware batching to avoid blocking allocation paths. - Add new metrics: kv_cache.fragmentation_score, kv_cache.defrag_attempts, kv_cache.spill_io_latency_p50/p95, kv_cache.eviction_reclaim_bytes. - Tests and benchmarks: microbenchmarks for allocation latency, end-to-end perf canary runs using long-context chat workloads, and regression tests for correctness under concurrent access.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-2140) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Benchmarks and perf numbers attached - [x] CI green after reruns - [x] Release notes included

Related: Linear ENG-2140, ENG-1254. Follow-up work: make defrag cost model pluggable and tune per-hardware profiles (separate PR).

review_comments: Maya Singh: Can you add a regression test that simulates high-allocation churn with small tensors? We need to ensure defrag doesn't thrash allocations.
Ethan Brooks: Added a microbenchmark and a synthetic regression test (tests/kv_cache_eviction_test.cc). The scheduler uses an adaptive backoff to avoid thrashing.
Ravi Patel: The spill-to-disk path needs to avoid blocking the allocation hot path; please confirm IO is off the critical path.
Ethan Brooks: Spill IO is now fully async and batched; allocation path only enqueues and returns. Added backpressure metrics to monitor queue growth.
Claire Nguyen: Can we surface the fragmentation score in the console and add an alert playbook?
Ethan Brooks: Added metrics and a draft dashboard JSON; added playbook notes to docs/eviction_policy.md.
Maya Singh: Benchmarks look good, p95 latency down ~18% under our long-context canary, please include the raw numbers in the PR description.

release_notes:
- Improved KV cache eviction and defragmentation heuristics to reduce tail-latency and memory pressure.
- Added fragmentation scoring and a throttled defrag scheduler.
- Async spillover I/O with batching to reduce allocation path stalls.
- New metrics for fragmentation and spill IO latency.
merge_commit_message:
squash: kv-cache: improve defrag and spillover heuristics (ENG-2140)

Combines fragmentation scoring, a throttled defrag scheduler, and async spill I/O to reduce tail-latency and memory pressure. Adds metrics and tests.
notes: Deployment: rolling rollout behind feature flag kv_cache.defrag_v6; gate enabled for dedicated pools first. Monitor kv_cache.fragmentation_score and kv_cache.eviction_reclaim_bytes during rollout. Will coordinate with SRE for canary windows.
